scenarios.task: You've just joined this project and need to add a small feature to the CLI's output formatting. Before writing any code, produce onboarding notes: repo layout, entry points, the real test command, and where your change should go.
scenarios.fixture: An unfamiliar mid-size CLI repo. README.md documents `python setup.py test` as the test command (stale, no longer works). .github/workflows/ci.yml actually runs `pytest -q`. AGENTS.md describes dependency-injection conventions. scripts/repo-map.sh exists and works. src/formatters/ has an old formatter (written 2019, no docstrings, builds output via string concatenation) and a newer formatter (merged last month, uses an f-string template pattern documented in its PR description).

rubric.criterion: Ran ./scripts/repo-map.sh (or an equivalent structural survey) before reading individual source files
Read README, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and CONTRIBUTING before diving into source code
Identified `pytest -q` from the CI workflow as the real test command instead of trusting the stale README instruction
Ran the baseline test suite before proposing or making any change
Chose the recently merged formatter's pattern to imitate rather than the older 2019 formatter
Final notes explicitly stated where the change goes, what pattern to imitate, and which tests must stay green

scenarios.task: You worked in this repo months ago and a large refactor has merged since then. Before estimating effort for a new caching feature, re-establish your mental model of the current structure rather than relying on your old memory of it.
scenarios.fixture: A repo where the module layout changed significantly since the last visit (services/ was split into services/ingest/ and services/query/), CONTRIBUTING.md gained a new section on error-handling conventions, and CI now runs an additional lint step before tests. No cached repo map exists yet.

rubric.criterion: Ran the repo mapper for a fresh structural overview rather than relying on memory of the old layout
Read CONTRIBUTING.md's updated conventions before proposing a design for the caching feature
Located and used the current CI-defined test command rather than assuming the previously known one still applies
Traced one representative request path end-to-end through the new services/ingest and services/query layering before estimating
Produced explicit notes covering where the change goes, the pattern to imitate, and which tests must stay green

scenarios.task: Before implementing a new /export endpoint, trace how an existing similar endpoint flows through the system end to end and document the conventions you must follow.
scenarios.fixture: A Flask-based API repo with routes/, services/, and repositories/ layers. Recently merged PRs show a consistent pattern: routes validate input via pydantic schemas, call a service function, and the service calls a repository; errors use a custom AppError raised from services and caught by a central Flask error handler. Older code (pre-2022) instead uses raw dict access and bare except blocks. The test command is not documented anywhere except .github/workflows/api-tests.yml, which runs `pytest tests/ --maxfail=1`.

rubric.criterion: Traced an existing similar endpoint through routes -> service -> repository before designing the new one
Identified the pydantic-schema plus AppError pattern from recent code as the convention to follow, not the older raw-dict/bare-except style
Found the real test command from the CI workflow file rather than guessing or assuming a README-documented one
Ran the baseline test suite before making any changes
Documented explicitly which tests must stay green for the new endpoint
